BLOCKER: `rehearsal()` in `pfaudit-swap/main.go` calls `list.Output()` (which blocks until `pg_restore -l` finishes reading its stdin) *before* `dec.Start()`; nothing has started writing to the pipe yet, so the rehearsal deadlocks every time it runs.

The rehearsal asserts the dump contains `"SEQUENCE public audit_legacy_id_seq"`, but `backup()` dumps `-t audit_id_seq` (the *new* shadow sequence) — the legacy sequence is never in the dump, so the rehearsal can never pass even after the deadlock is fixed.

`PostVerify` runs *after* the swap transaction commits and compares `audit_legacy` vs `audit` row-for-row; any concurrent insert between commit and verify causes a spurious mismatch that blocks the documented crash-resume path.
MAJOR: `checksumExpr` uses `hashtextextended` (a 64-bit order-independent sum), not the SHA-256-over-ordered-rows digest the AC and `EDP-17-SCHEMA.md` both promise; the advertised integrity guarantee is materially weaker than documented.

`RestoreMonth` attaches an `audit_restore_YYYYMM` partition to the live parent with the same range as the original month and never detaches/drops it; the next `audit_ensure_partitions` call will hit a 23P01 range-overlap failure for that month.

No code rejects a legal hold recorded against a purged month or emits `audit_hold_after_purge_total`; the AC and ADR both promise this spoliation guard but it is absent from the migration and the Go tooling.
`PurgeMonth` deletes object-store keys *before* `audit_mark_purged`; a crash in between leaves purged data with a manifest still marked un-purged and no durable purge record.
`close` calls `obj.Delete` on the encrypted backup *before* `RecordState(..., "swap_closed", ...)`; if the state write fails the backup is destroyed with no audit trail of the sign-off.
`S3Store.Put` buffers the entire object via `io.ReadAll` before upload, so the pre-swap `pg_dump` of a large audit table will OOM rather than stream.
MINOR: `audit_append_late` inserts into the canonical `audit_YYYYMM` partition, not a distinct `audit_late_YYYYMM` partition as the AC and `EDP-17-SCHEMA.md` describe; docs and implementation disagree.
`architect_review.py` is modified in the same diff to force the review output format and raise the diff limit; scope creep that changes the review gate alongside the feature.
Metrics JSON is emitted to stdout mixed with human-readable progress lines, making reliable ops parsing difficult.
`s3store` SSE-KMS path does not validate that `aws:kms:` includes a non-empty key ID before calling `NewSSEKMS`.

Several declared metric constants (`MetricInsertOutOfRange`, `MetricProvisionSeconds`, `MetricCopyResumed`, `MetricDrop`, `MetricLateInsert`, `MetricHoldAfterPurge`, `MetricHoldExtractFailed`) are never emitted anywhere in the diff.
`audit_drop_partition`'s row-count cross-check will permanently block retention of any month that received a late insert after export; no reconcile path is provided.
NIT: `Down` copies back post-swap rows but does not explicitly re-advance `audit_legacy_id_seq` before the rename; the later `setval` covers it but the intermediate state is briefly inconsistent.
`pfaudit-retention` acquires the `AURE` advisory lock on a dedicated connection but performs all work on other pool connections; the lock serializes runs but does not protect the work itself.
`ExportMonth`'s role check requires `rolsuper OR rolbypassrls`; if `pf_owner` is neither, export always fails and no alternative is documented.
SUMMARY: The diff delivers a large, well-structured partitioning and retention substrate but contains several objectively verifiable correctness defects that block merge: a guaranteed deadlock in the backup rehearsal, a rehearsal assertion that can never pass against the actual dump contents, and a post-swap verification step that races with live inserts.
The integrity primitive advertised as SHA-256 is in fact a 64-bit hash, and the documented spoliation guard for holds-after-purge is entirely absent.
Restore leaves an orphaned partition that will break future rotation, and purge/close both destroy data before durably recording the action.
These must be fixed before the swap and retention paths are trusted in production.
